These are reserved areas which are development of fauna and their natural habitat National Parks of Odisha A national park is a reserved area of natural restricted from any kind of encroachment and National Parks in Odisha as per the report (ENVIS) centre on Wildlife and Protected discussed below: Bhitarkanika National Park It is located on the North-East of Kendrapara l existence in the year 1998. This national Wildlife Sanctuary. It covers an area of 145 protected areas of the state. It is rich in reptiles, mammals and birds. l Thespia, Teak, Salaia, Bamboo, Babool, Important fauna found here are crocodile, l cobra, black ibis and many other species of and birds. AND flora and fauna. There are parks in the state. The sanctuaries of the state are National Park, Badrama Balukhand Konark Sanctuary, etc. shelter to a rich flora and fauna of used for the protection and and environment. land owned by government, that is development. It is one of the five marine Important flora of this park are Sundari, Palas, Indigo bush, etc. white crocodile, Indian python, king fauna. It has many species of plants 118 Simlipal National Park It is located in Mayurbhanj district in l the North-Eastern part of Odisha. It is situated at a distance of 320 km from Bhubaneswar. It came into existence in 1980. It covers an area of 845.70 sq km. It is l surrounded by deciduous trees and sal forests. Twelve rivers run across this national park, e.g. Budhabalanga, Palpala, Deo river, etc. It has a unique feature of being a tiger l reserve, a sanctuary and a biosphere reserve. The park has a mixed type of l vegetation with Northern tropical semi-evergreen trees and Northern tropical moist deciduous trees and orchids. Savannas and grasslands provide grazing grounds to its fauna. The park is a viable source for many medicinal and aromatic plants also. It is home to animals like tiger, Asian l elephant and gaur (Indian bison). Other animals such as four-horned antelope, deer, leopard, bear, spotted deer and barking deer, sambars deer, langurs, etc. are found here. It provides shelter to Royal Bengal l Tigers. The park also has Joranda (150 m) and Barehipani (400 m) waterfalls. Wildlife Sanctuaries of Odisha Wildlife Sanctuary is an area which is protected but allows little human activities for protecting and developing wildlife. Odisha has 19 wildlife sanctuaries as per the report of ENVIS centre on Wildlife and Protected Areas, Government of India. The largest Wildlife Sanctuary in Odisha is Gahirmatha Wildlife Sanctuary and the smallest Wildlife Sanctuary is Nandankanan Wildlife Sanctuary. Some major wildlife sanctuaries in Odisha are as follows: Badrama Wildlife Sanctuary It is also known as Ushakothi l Sanctuary. It is located in Sambalpur district. It came into existence in 1962 and covers an area of 304.03 sq km. It is comprised of parts of Badrama l Reserve Forests, Ushakothi Reserve Forests, Binjipali Reserve Forests and Kansar Reserve Forests. Important flora of the sanctuary are l moist sal forests, sal dominated mixed deciduous forests and bamboo forests. Important fauna are tiger, elephant, l leopard, hyena, bison, wildboar, spotted deer, sambar deer, bear, porcupine, and many varieties of birds and reptiles. Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in the estuarine region of l Brahmani-Baitarani rivers in the North-Eastern corner of Kendrapara district. It came into existence in the year 1975 and covers an area of 525 sq km. The sanctuary has mangrove forests and is cris-crossed by tidal inundated creeks. This sanctuary is bordered by sea l beach, which attracts thousands of Olive Ridley sea turtles during January to April. National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries Important fauna of this sanctuary are l salt water crocodile (endangered), hyena, fishing cat, jungle cat, civet, Indian porcupine, wild boar, spotted deer, sambar, stork, Asian open bill, egrets, black ibis, cormorants, darters, etc. Satkosia Gorge Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Angul district and is l adjoined by Boudh Nayagarh and Cuttack districts. It came into existence in 1976 and covers an area of 745.52 sq km. The Satkosia Gorge is part of an extension of Mahanadi river. Important flora of the sanctuary are l mixed deciduous forests, sal and riverine forests. Important fauna are gharials, elephant, l leopard, gaur, black bear, slow loris, musk deer, wild goat, Assamese macaque, pig-tailed macaque, etc. Some major attractions in this l sanctuary are Satkosia Gorge, the Gharial Research and Conservation Unit at Tikarapada, hill slopes, various tracking routes and boating. Simlipal Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Mayurbhanj district. It l came into existence in the year 1979. It covers an area of 1354 sq km. Important flora of this sanctuary are l sal forests, semi-evergreen forests and tropical moist deciduous forests. Important fauna of this sanctuary are l tigers, elephants, panthers, gaurs, pangolins, four horned antelopes, red jungle fowl, crested serpent eagle, grey hornbill, peafowl, Indian hill myna, etc. in Odisha 119 Nandankanan Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Khurda district amidst l of Chandaka forests. It came into existence in the year 1979. It covers an area of 14.16 sq km. It is the only conservation breeding l centre of Indian pangolins in the world. It has been internationally acclaimed l for its highest collection of white tigers in the world. Besides white tigers and gharials, leopard, mouse deer, lions, ratel and vultures are found here. The fauna of this sanctuary are Asiatic l lion, Indian crocodiles, lion, tailed macaque, Nilgiri langur, Indian pangolin, mouse deer, etc. Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Nayagarh district. It l came into existence in the year 1981. It covers an area around 168.35 sq km. It has a close proximity with the Satkosia Gorge Sanctuary. It is situated in the Eastern highlands l moist deciduous forests eco-region. Important flora of this sanctuary are l mixed deciduous forests, dry deciduous forests and moist Peninsular sal forests. Important fauna are elephants, tigers, l leopards, water birds and some varieties of reptiles like python, king cobra, etc. Chandaka Dampara Wildlife Sanctuary It is located partly in Khurda district l and partly in Cuttack district. It came into existence and designated as an elephant reserve in 1982. It covers an area of 175.79 sq km. 120 Important flora of this sanctuary are l moist semi-evergreen forests, moist Kangada forests, coastal sal forests, thorny bamboo forests, planted teak, scrub, orchids, etc. Important fauna are Indian elephant, l leopard, chital, barking deer, mouse deer, wild pig, common langur, small Indian civet, pangolin, sloth bear, hyena, peafowl, red jungle fowl, crested serpent eagle and many reptiles. Balukhand-Konark Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Puri district along sea l coast between Puri and Konark. It came into existence in the year 1984. It covers an area of 71.72 sq km. It is the ideal habitat of the Chousingha. The combination of dry deciduous l mixed forests with rich wildlife and Hirakud reservoir, are some important features of Balukhand-Konark Wildlife Sanctuary. Important fauna of this sanctuary are l black buck, spotted deer, monkey, squirrel, jungle cat, hyena, mongoose, jackal and many varieties of birds and reptiles. Chilika Wildlife Sanctuary It is located on the east coast of Puri, l Khurda and Ganjam district. It came into existence in 1987. It covers an area of about 15.53 sq km. It is also known as Nalabana Bird Sanctuary and it is an island in Chilika lake. This area is completely submerged l during the monsoon season. This sanctuary comprises of 60% of the total migratory bird species visiting Chilika lake each year. Birds Island is a part of this lake which l is known as heaven for the resident and migratory birds. It is a home to endangered Irrawady l dolphins and bottle-nosed dolphins also can be seen. Important birds species of this l sanctuary are white bellied sea eagles, greylag geese, purple moorhen, jacana, herons, flamingos. Important fauna are black buck, l spotted deer, jungle cat, fox, golden jackals, hyena, etc. The sanctuary also has about 160 species of fishes. Sunabeda Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Nuapada district. It l came into existence in the year 1988 and covers an area of 500 sq km. It adjoins the Sitanadi and Udanti Sanctuaries of Chhattisgarh. It has eleven beautiful waterfalls and l seasonal streams. Important fauna of this sanctuary are swamp deer, wild water buffalo, tiger, leopard, hyena, gaur, barking and spotted deer, nilgai, etc. The varieties of birds, around 200 l species, such as hill myna, peafowl, partridge and also number of reptilian species are also found here. The National Tiger Conservation l Authority selected it as Tiger Reserve. This sanctuary is an ideal habitat for l Barasingha. It also forms a migration link for wild l buffaloes across two Indian states, i.e. Odisha and Chhattisgarh. National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries Gahirmatha (Marine) Wildlife Sanctuary It is located in Kendrapara district of l Odisha. It came into existence in 1997. It covers an area of 1435 sq km. This is the world’s largest nesting beach of Olive Ridley Sea Turtles. Important flora of the sanctuary are l bel, tendu, hiwar, palas, sal, dhawda, babool, teak, bamboo, etc. Important fauna are wild boar, l bear, barking deer, leopard, jungle fowl, crocodile, sambar, hyena, wild dog, four-horned antelope, chinkara, etc. Other Wildlife Sanctuaries Wildlife Area Year Place Sanctuary (sq km) Debrigarh Wildlife 1985 Sambalpur 346.91 Sanctuary Hadgarh Wildlife 1978 Keonjhar 191.06 Sanctuary Karlapat Wildlife 1992 Kalahandi 147.66 Sanctuary Khalasuni Wildlife 1982 Sambalpur 116 Sanctuary Kotagarh Wildlife 1981 Kandhamal 399.5 Sanctuary Kuldiha Wildlife 1984 Balasore 272.75 Sanctuary Lakhari Wildlife 1985 Ganjam 185.87 Sanctuary Kapilasa Wildlife 2011 Dhenkanal 125.5 Sanctuary Wildlife Reserves in Odisha Wildlife reserve is a protected area for wildlife, flora and fauna. It is reserved and managed for conservation and to provide opportunities for research work for a particular species. in Odisha 121 Some major wildlife reserves of Odisha are discussed below: Simlipal Tiger Reserve It is located in Mayurbhanj district of l Odisha. It came into existence in 1956. It covers an area around 2,750 sq km. This reserve was selected as one amongst the 9 reserves for implementation of the first phase of Project Tiger in 1973. After the launch of this project, the number of tigers has increased. The reserve has around 1,352 plant l species with 94 species of orchids of which 35 species of Odisha are endemic to Simlipal. It has semi- evergreen and moist deciduous forests. Important fauna are leopard, sambar, l langur, deer, gaur (Indian bison), elephant, antelope, cheetal, wild dog, wild boar, sloth bear, monkey, hyena and porcupine, etc. Mayurbhanj Elephant Reserve It is located on the borders of l Mayurbhanj, Balasore, Bhadrak and Keonjhar district. This elephant reserve comprises of three protected areas such as Simlipal Tiger Reserve, Hadgarh Wildlife Sanctuary and Kuldiha Wildlife Sanctuary. It came into existence in the year 2001. l It covers an area of 3,214 sq km. The reserve also includes the reserve l forests, protected forests, private lands and revenue lands. It has mainly constituted for elephants. The main feature of this reserve is the l Hadgarh Sanctuary and the reservoir of Hadgarh, which is adjoining with Baula Hills. This reservoir is built on Salandi river. 122 Mahanadi Elephant Reserve It is located on the borders of Angul, l Cuttack, Nayagarh, Kandhamal and Dhenkanal district. It came into existence in 2002. It covers an area of 1,038 sq km. It comprises of the forest divisions of l portions of Angul, Athagarh, Cuttack, Nayagarh, Boudh and Dhenkanal, and entire Satkosi Wilidlife Division, Mahanadi Wildlife division and Athamalik forest division. Sambalpur Elephant Reserve It is located on the coast of l Sambalpur, Sundargarh, and Jharsuguda district and is a part of Badrama Wildlife Sanctuary. It came into existence in the year 2002. It covers an area of 427 sq km. It comprises of the forest divisions of l (parts) Bamra, Bonai, Sambalpur, Jharsuguda and Rairakhol. Satkosia Tiger Reserve It is located in the central zone of the l state and spreads over Cuttack, Nayagarh, Angul, and Boudh districts. It came into existence in the year 2007. It covers an area of 963.87 sq km. l This tiger reserve is comprised of Satkosia Gorge Wildlife Sanctuary and Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary. It is a home to the most endangered l gharial, the mugger, crocodiles and this reserve also has a variety of freshwater turtles. Important flora of this reserve are l moist deciduous forests, dry mixed deciduous forest, bamboo brakes, dry tropical riparian forest and teak plantations. Important fauna are leopard, wild dog, l nilgai, sambar, spotted deer, barking deer, bear, jackal, porcupine, Indian hare, giant squirrel, etc. This reserve is home to around 155 l elephants which also forms a part of Mahanadi Elephant Reserve. The reserve also has migratory birds l species, like Hornbills, Peafowl, Kingfisher, Cormorant, River tern, Owl, Myna, Bar headed Geese, etc. The reserve also has the high vulnerable species of Indian skimmers flocks. Biodiversity in Odisha Odisha has a rich biodiversity. The largest Ramsar sites (brackish water Chilika lake and the mangrove forests of Bhitarkanika), attract the largest population of migratory birds from distant lands. The floral and faunal diversity of Simlipal biosphere, rich medicinal plants in Simlipal Gandhamardhan forest ranges and many tribal races are an important part of biodiversity in Odisha. Major biodiversity hotspots in Odisha are as follows: Simlipal Biosphere Reserve The Simlipal area lies on the l Northern limit of Deccan plateau and Southern limit of lower Gangetic plains adjoining Chota Nagpur highlands. The Simlipal Biosphere Reserve is l located in Mayurbhanj district. It came into existence in 1994 and covers an area of 4,374 sq km. National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries It comprises Northern tropical l semi-evergreen forest, Northern tropical moist deciduous forest, dry deciduous hill forests, high level sal forests, grassland and Savannah. It includes the entire Simlipal l Sanctuary and the adjoining Nato and Satkosia Reserve Forests. In this biosphere reserve, tiger population l is over 50% of the entire tiger population of Odisha state. It has more than 200 species of medicinal plants. Important fauna are elephant, tigers, l leopard, four-horned antelope. This region also has the famous Hirakud Dam reservoir. The forest tree vegetation is categorised l as Shorea terminalia. The area is also significant for large wildlife. The Gandhamardan hill range has very rich medicinal flora. The area comprises semi-evergreen forests, dry deciduous dense forests, bamboo forests, dry deciduous open forests, scrub wood land, barren rocky areas, etc. Bhitarkanika Mangrove The mangrove forests of Bhitarkanika l are located in the Brahmani, Baitarani and Dhamra rivers deltaic regions. It covers an area of 3000 sq km. It has the second largest mangroves forest after Sundarbans of West Bengal. in Odisha 123 This deltaic region has large number l of creeks and rivulets. He was a 12th century poet. He is known all over the world for his epic ‘Geeta Govinda’ which highlights Krishna’s love with Radha. He greatly contributed to the Odissi music. He also institutionalised the ‘Debadasi’ system in Odia temples. Geeta Govinda has now become the main support around which Odissi dance is based and also has a great influence on Patta paintings of Odisha. He died in 1245 AD. Sarala Das He was born in 15th century. He is also called ‘Utkal Balmiki’ and ‘Adikari’. He is the author of Vilanka Ramayana Chandipurana and Odia Mahabharata. The Odia language emerged in its present form by the contributions of Sarala Das. Sometimes Odia literature is also classified as Pre Sarala Yug, Sarala Yug and Post Sarala Yug. Deenakrushna Das He was born in 1650 AD in Balasore district of Odisha. He is famous for his composition ‘Rasakallola’ that beautifully creates the divine leela of Radha and Krishna. His other works include Rasa Binoda, Amruta Sagar, Guna Sagar, Bhabha Samudra, etc. He died in 1710 AD. 257 Upendra Bhanja He was born in 1670 AD at Bhanjanagar, 80 km from Berhampur city. He is considered greatest poet of Odia literature and is also known as Kabi-Samrat or Greatest poet of Ritiyuga. His famous works are Labanyabati, Brajaleela, Baidehisha Bilasa, Rasapanchaka, etc. He is also credited with writing the first Odia dictionary Gita Abidhan. He contributed 32,300 words to Odia language and literature. His style of writing Sanskrit poetics is called Reeti and Deena. Brajanath Badajena He was born in 1730 AD in Kabara village of Dhenkanal district. He was an eminent writer of Riti Yuga and a contemporary of Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja. His poetic creations in Odia include ‘Keli Kalanidhi’, ‘Bidesh’, ‘Gopi Bilapa, etc. His composition in Sanskrit is ‘Manoduta’ and in Hindi is ‘Gundichabije’. He died in 1800 AD. Kavisurya Baladev Rath He was born in 1789 AD in Badakhemundi of Ganjam district. He was a poet and laureate. His creations include ‘Kavisurya Granthavali’, ‘Kavisurya Geetavali’, ‘Kishore Chandranana’, ‘Chaupadi Chautisha’, etc. He founded Dhumpa Sangita. He died in 1845. Gourishankar Ray He was born on 13th July, 1839 in Cuttack district. He was also known as ‘Karmaveer Gourishankar’. 258 He was one of the prominent personalities for making the state of modern Odisha and was the saviour of Odia language and literature. He led the Save Odia Movement during the late 19th century and worked hard for the protection and preservation of the Odia language. He founded the Cuttack Printing Company and was the editor of Utkal Deepika (first Odia newspaper). He died on 7th March, 1917. Bhima Bhoi He was born in 1850 in Sambalpur district of Odisha. He was blind from birth. With the blessings of his guru, Mahima Mahaprabhu, he wrote about sufferings of humanity, spiritualism and philosophy. He renounced worship of idols as they are mere wooden or metal statues and encouraged people to serve humanity. His works include ‘Stuti Chintamani’, ‘Brahma Nirupana Geeta’, ‘Nirbeda Sadhana’, ‘Adi Anta Geeta’, etc. He died in 1895. Nanda Kishore Bal He was born on 22nd December, 1875 at Kusupur village of Cuttack district. He was a great poet, who presented a lively picture of rural Odisha in his poems. He is popularly known as Palli Kabi. His poetic creations, Pallichitra, Nirjharini, Basanta–Kokila, Tarangini, Charuchitra, Nirmalaya, Prabhata Sangeeta, Sandhya Sangita, Nana Baya Gita, Krushna Kumari, Sharmistha and novel Kanakalata are very popular among readers. He died on 1st July, 1928. Utkalmani Gopabandhu Das He born in 1877 in Puri district. He was one of the founders of the modern Odisha state. He is also remembered for his patriotic lyrical poems and lucid, thought provoking prose writings. He started the weekly newspaper ‘The Samaja’ in 1919. He died in 1928. Godabarish Mohapatra He was born on 26th October, 1886 in Khordha district. He was an inspiring writer and a prominent freedom fighter. He published his own magazine ‘Niakunta’ (1938) and ‘Tuan Tuin Tuin’ (1957). He received Odia Sahitya Akademi Award for his revolutionary work ‘Mo Khelasathi’, ‘Utha Kankala’ and ‘Kanta O Phula’. He also received the Central Sahitya Akademi Award. He died on 26 July, 1956. Kabai Chandra Kalicharan Patnaik He was born in 23 December, 1897 in Banki of Cuttack district. He is known for his drama literature in Odia language. He wrote mythological, historical, social dramas and dramas based on different characters. He also wrote stories, poems and one-act plays. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1971. Due to his great contribution in drama, Sri Ramachandra Dev, Gajapati of Puri, gave him the title of ‘Kabichandra’ in 1927. His works include Mrugaya, Sakuntala, Harishchandra, Abhijana, Rakta Mandara, Jayadeva, Pratisodha, Ahuti, Banaphula, Ananga, Jugapurusha, etc. He died in 1978. Language and Literature Annada Shankar Ray He was born in 1904 in Dhenkanal district. He was Bengali poet and essayist who also wrote for Odia poetry. He received many awards like Padma Bhushan, Sahitya Akademi Award etc. His important literary works are Du Kankata, Binur Boi, Japane, Konna, Tarunno. He died in 2002. Jayanta Mahapatra He was born in 1928 in Cuttack district. He is one of the best known Indian English poets. He has won prominence for his powerful, haunting and visionary works. His literary works are like, ‘A Rain of Rites,’, ‘A Father’s Hours’, ‘The Green Gardener’, ‘Baya Raja’, ‘Smruti Pari Kichhiti’, etc. He has authored 27 books of poems, of which 7 are in Odia and the rest in English. Manoj Das He was born in Balasore district in 1934. Saraswati Samman Award winner, Professor Manoj Das is one of the foremost short story writers in post-Independence India. His works include short stories, poems, travelogues and essays in both English and Odia. 259 His prominent works are Kete Diganta, Kabita Utkala, Amruta Phala, etc. He also received Padma Shri in 2001. Sitakant Mahapatra He was born in 1937 in Cuttack district of Odisha. He is a notable Indian poet and literary critic in Odia and English. He is awarded with a number of awards like, Jnanpith Award (1993), Sahitya Akademi Award (1974), Padma Bhushan (2002) and Padma Vibhusan (2010). His notable works include ‘Ashtapadi’ (1963), ‘Shabdara Akash’ (1971), ‘Unending Rhythms’ (Oral poetry of Santhal tribes), etc. Pratibha Ray She was born in 1943 in Jagatsinghpur district. She is one of the most famous writers in Odisha. She has been writing novels and short stories actively for the past 25 years. She has received many awards like Odisha Sahitya Akademi Awards, Padma Shri Award, Jnanpith Award, etc. Her important works are Gandhinka, Gangashiuli, Dura Dwividha, Barsa Basanta Baishakha, etc. 260 Prominent Authors and Their Important Books Name Gita Govinda Odia Mahabharata Keshaba Koili Dandi Ramayan, Amar Kosh Shreemada Bhagawat Hari Bansa Govinda Chandra Nrusingh Purana Rukumini Bibhaha Raghunatha Bilash Rasa Kallola Baidehi Bilasa (Labanyabati) Bidgadha Chintamani Kabita Kallohla, Kishore Chandranan Champu Stuti Chintamani, Adianta Gita Mahamoha, Janjyaseni and Silapadma Bandira Atmakatha, Kara Kabita Tapaswaini, Pranaya Bhallari Amritua Santa, Mati o Matala Bajare Bajabala Sri Radha, Aneka Kothari, Saptaima Rutu Belun Gala Udi Jhumuka Ara Drushya Ashwamedheva Ghoda Amabasyara Chandra Bhool Prutibira Tire Baji Rout, Pandulipi Bruhat Srishal Itihas Andha Gali Bana Raijara Katha Compositions Author’s Name Jayadev Sarala Das Markanda Das Balaram Das Jagannath Das Achyutananda Das Yosabanta Das Pitambar Das Kartika Das Dhananjaya Bhanja Dinakrushna Das Upendra Bhanja Abhimanyu Samant Singhar Kabisurya Baladev Ratha Bhima Bhoi Pratibha Ray Gopabandhu Das Gandhar Meher Gopinath Mohanty Ramprasad Mohanty Ramkanta Rath Maheswar Mohanty Rama Krushna Nanda Sitakant Mahapatra Bibhuti Patnaik Govinda Das Nityananda Mahapatra Debaraj Lenka Sachidanand Routray Ramchandra Mallick Akhil Mohan Patnaik Manorama Mohapatra Language and Literature

The Chaurisha represents the originality of Odissi style. In the Chhandas, the thirty-four letters of the Odia alphabet from ‘Ka’ to ‘Ksha’ are used chronologically at the beginning of each line. Unlike Hindustani and Odissi Ragas Carnatic music, Odissi ragas have different style. Kalyana, Nata, Shree Gowda, Baradi, Panchama, Dhanashri, Karnata, Bhairavee and Shokabaradi are chief Odissi ragas. The greatest exponents of Odissi music in modern times are the late Singhari Shyamasundar Kar, Markandeya Mahapatra, Kashinath Pujapanda, Balakrushna Das, Bhubaneswari Mishra, Shyamamani Devi and Sunanda Patnaik. Musical Traditions of Odisha The present musical tradition (Gharanas) of Odisha can be broadly grouped under the following categories: Classical Music It is the traditional music of Odisha. It consists of Anirjukta Pravadha, Sri Geetagovinda, Divya Manusi, Prabandha, Chhander, Chautisa. Chaupadi (Odissi), Malasri, Sariman, Champu Vyanjani, Chaturang, Tribhang, Kuduka Geeta, Swarnamalya and Laxana. Light Classical Music It is consisted of Bhajan, Janam, Odiya songs based on Ragas, Rangila Chaupadi, etc. 277 Folk Music This music is the expression of the ethos and moves of the folk people. Important folk music are Geeta, Balipuja Geeta, Kela Keluni Geeta, Dalkhai Geeta, Kendra Geeta, Jaiphula Geeta, Ghoda Nacha, Danda Nacha Geeta, Ghumura Geeta, Gopal Ugala and Osa-Parva Geeta. Tribal music This type of music is associated with the tribal population of the state especially in the hilly forest regions and coastal belt region. Musical Instruments of Odisha Various musical instruments accompany the music and dance performances of Odisha. The Baunsa Taranga and Katha Taranga are the indigenous musical instruments in Odisha. Many musical instruments like Khanjani, Dholki, Madala, Ghumura and Pakhawaj are played during festivals that echo the feeling of joy. Musical Instruments like Flute, Dhanakoila, Behela and Kendera are used during the moment of sorrow and grief. The conchshells represent good omens and are played in marriages, auspicious occasions and invoking the deities. Stringed musical instruments like Veena, Sarangi, Ektara, Behela and Dhenka are well-known throughout the state. Other important instruments are Tamak, Mahuri,Gochi baja, Ghanta, etc. 278 Some famous musical instruments of Odisha are discussed below: Tamak It is one of a traditional instrument of the state. It consists of animal skin stretched over a wooden base. The membrane is vibrated with two long wooden sticks. It is usually played in marriage processions and on other festive occassions. Mahuri It is a traditional wind instrument belonging to the state. It is an auspicious instrument. It is played during marriages. It is also used in folk theatres like Rama Nataka and dances like Chhau. Gochi Baja It is a traditional percussion instrument belonging to the state. It is considered auspicious and is usually played in marriage processions. Kendera It is an ethnic stringed instrument ritually used by ascetics of the Nâtha sect while gathering alms. It is normally made of a coconut shell on which the skin of a monitor lizard has been stretched. A bamboo stick is used as the bow for the instrument. Ghanta It is a metallic gong used as a percussion instrument. It is used during the majestic Ratha Jatra of Puri in which hundreds of ghantas play in a synchronised beat with fervour, dramatically swinging their torsos back and forth. Odisha is a land of different dance forms, which ranges from classical, tribal and folk dances. The famous dance forms of Odisha are discussed below: Odissi Dance This is one of the eight acknowledged l classical dance forms of India and the most famous dance of Odisha. Like all other Indian classical dances, l it also has its initiation in religion and philosophy with an origin in the temples of Odisha. The rhythm, and mudras used in l Odissi dance have a distinct style of its own. The dance depicts the theme of l infinite love of Lord Krishna and Radha. This dance has a long history but it l got its recognition as a classical dance only in the year 1958. Odissi includes both Tandava and l Lasya elements and has navatala system. In Odissi, the torso movement is l considered very important which is soft, lyrical and graceful. Music and Dance of Odisha The basic body position is chowka that is l Jagannath’s body position. The dance has a mention in Bharata Natyashastra l Odissi dance style comprises of the following l Batu Nrutya, Pallavi, Abhinaya and Moksha. Dancers wear queens. and mostly performed in Puri. region in the districts of Sambalpur and 284 Folk Dramas of Odisha There are different types of the theortical performances/ folk dramas in Odisha which are discussed as follows: Chadheya Nata This is a folk drama of Odisha which l is very prevalent in the districts of Mayurbhanj and Balasore. This play consists of three characters, namely, the Chadheya, the Chadheyani (Wife of Chadheya) and Banku Bhai (the Joker). This folk drama is accompanied by a l chorus group songs with musical instruments. ‘Mausa’ is the chief of this drama who interprets the play and controls the performances. Daskathia This folk drama is mainly associated l with the worship of Lord Shiva and thus, the performers mention its various forms like Rudra, Hara, Mahadeva, Shankar, etc. The folk drama mainly belongs to l Ganjam district but now it is observed in all other districts of Odisha. The meaning of ‘Dasa’ is a devotee l and ‘Kathia’ is two wooden pieces which are used to play tune during the prayer by the devotee. It is a two persons act which consists l of chief singer, (Gayaka) and the other person known as ‘Palia’ who helps the chief singer during singing and acting. They introduce humorous stories in between the drama. Dhanu Yatra This moving drama/theatre is very l prevalent in the districts of Bargarh and Sambalpur in Odisha. It is based on Krishna Leela and is held for eleven days. It is about the episode of Krishna and l Balaram’s visit to Mathura to witness the Dhanu ceremony organised by their (maternal) uncle Kansa. The play starts with the dethroning of l emperor Ugrasena by the angry prince Kansa, over the marriage of his sister Debaki with Basudeba and ends with death of Kansa and Ugrasen restoring back to become the king. There is no written script used in these enactments. Jatra It is also known as Gananatya or Opera l Nacha in Odisha. It is a song, dance, acting and musical theatre which is accompanied with many musical instruments like, Harmonium, Clarinet, Bugle, Mridanga, Jhanja, Dubi table, Dholki, etc. It is performed in an open field. This drama depicts a range of diverse l and complex stories from mythology, secular themes, humour, valour of heroic characters and melodramatic events. The drama is played in a rectangular l stage which is set in the centre of the audience along with the orchestra sitting adjacent to the stage. In this folk drama male persons are l dressed up like females. ‘Duari’ or ‘Dagara’ (the messenger of the king) and joker are the very interesting characters of this play. Music and Dance of Odisha Leela It is a form of Opera which is based l on lives of Lord Krishna and Lord Rama. A chorus group narrates the different episodes of Lord Rama’s heroic acts in Ramleela and Krishna’s flirting with the Gopis and Radha in Rasleela. The pioneer of Leela tradition was l Jagannath Das. It is prevalent in Boudh, Cuttack, Ganjam and Nayagarh districts of Odisha. Mughal Tamasa It is a folk drama of Odisha which is l prevalent in Bhadrak and Balasore districts of Odisha. It is a form of opera based on Mughal administration which once ruled Odisha. The songs and dialogues of this drama l are composed in Oriya, Urdu and Persian languages. Late Bansiballav Goswami had written the Mughal Tamasa in 1728AD. Pala It is a musical dance folk drama which l is based an ancient Odia literature. This drama depicts the social harmony of Hindu and Muslims. In this dance, people worship Satyapeer where ‘Satya’ represents the Hindu god ‘Satyanarayana’ and ‘Peer’ represents ‘Muslims peer’. In this folk drama five to seven l members take part in which the leader is known as ‘Mukhia’ or ‘Mukhya Gayak’ who sings the song by waving the ‘Chamar’ (Whisk) and a small stick. 285 ‘Sri Palia’ is the main supporter of the l leader, the person who plays Mridanga is called ‘Bayak’ and rest of the members are called as ‘Palia’ (chorus) as they repeat the songs with the Mukhya Gayak and Sri Palia. The theme of this drama is based on l Ramayana or Mahabharata. In this drama two parties also l challenge each other. This is performed in many districts of Odisha like Balasore, Bhadrak, Cuttack, Dhenkanal, Deogarh, Jaipur, Jagatsinghpur, Jharsuguda, Kendrapara, Keonjhar and Khordha. Patua In this drama, songs are composed by l the village poets who pick up the themes from Mahabharata, Ramayana, Puranas and recent novels. The Ghanta Patuas are the traditional male folk artists in this drama who work as temple servants. The dance in this drama is dedicated l to goddesses Sarala, Charchika, Hingula, Bhagabati Mangala and Chandi. The male dancers perform in a group l of two or four by wearing female dresses. In this folk drama, Ghanta and Dhol l musical instruments are used. Patuas are of four types but all of them worship the same deity under different names. This is mainly performed in Cuttack, l Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts. 286 Prahlad Natak This play particularly belongs to l Ganjam district in South Odisha. It is based on ‘Prahlad’ and similar to Suanga folk drama. The drama consists of about twenty male characters, five female characters and a main singer leader and Sutradhara namely, ‘Gahaka’. The songs are hundred and twenty in l numbers which are composed in a particular Raga and Tala. Puppet Play It is a typical folk drama of Odisha, in which colourful dolls are used to represent various characters. There are four kinds of puppetry in Odisha such as: It is also known as Shadow Puppet ‘Ravana Chhaya’ in Odisha. It is based on stories of Lord Rama. The puppets are made of deer skin. Simple Odissi music is used. It is prevalent in Angul districts. String Puppet It is also known as Gopalila Puppet which is based on Lord Krishna. It is prevalent in Ganjam, Puri, Balasore and Cuttack districts. Glove Puppet It is also known as Sakhi Kundhei Nata in Odisha. In this show puppets are used as gloves and puppeteer dances and sings while playing them. It is prevalent in Khordha (Bhubaneswar) and Cuttack districts. Rod Puppet It is also known as Danda Kandhei in Odisha. In this show’ puppets are fixed at the one end of a rod and their hands and legs are flexible. This is found only in Keonjhar district of Odisha. Cultural Institutions in Odisha Important cultural institutions of Odisha are given below: Odisha Dance Academy This dance academy was established l by Guru Gangadhar Pradhan and Dhirendra Nath Patnaik in 1975 in Bhubaneswar. The aim of this academy is to l popularise Odissi dance and music, as well as imparting intensive training to artists both in India and abroad. This academy organises many cultural l festivals like Odissi, Sandhya and Annual festival of dance and music every year and it also started Konark dance and Music festival from 1986. It also organises Dhauli-Kalinga l Mahotsav at Shanti Vihar, Bhubaneswar from 6th to 8th February, every year. It also organises the Annual Festival in San Diego in collaboration with the Centre for World Music. Guru Kelu Charan Mohapatra Odissi Research Centre This research centre was established l by the State Government in the year 1986 by the name as ‘Odissi Research Centre’ in Bhubaneswar. Later, it was renamed as Guru Kelu l Charan Mohapatra Odissi Research Centre’ after the name of Late Guru Kelu Charan Mohapatra who devoted his entire life to promote this dance as a classical dance at the world level. Music and Dance of Odisha The aim of this centre is to promote l three styles of Odissi dance i.e. Guru Kelu Charan style, Guru Pankaj Charan style and Guru Deba Prasad style. It also aims to publish literature of l Indian and Odishan dance and music and sponsor Odissi dance and music festivals and competitions, to establish model institutions devoted to the teaching of and research in Odissi dance and music. Utkal University of Culture, Sanskruti Vihar This university was established on 9th l June, 1999 by the State Government as a teaching-cum affiliating university. It got the recognition by the l University Grants Commission (UGC) on 1st December, 1999. It is located in Bhubaneswar. The aim of this university is to engage l itself to preserve, promote, propagate and protect the richness of state’s cultural values through research, documentation and education. Abhima Sundar Gotipua Nrutya Parishad This traditional Gurukul was establis- l hed by Sri Laxman Maharana. It is located in Raghurajpur in Puri district. This Gurukul is working for the l promotion and popularisation of the Gotipua, which is a traditional dance of Odisha state. Srajan-Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi Nrityabasa This Odissi dance school was founded l by Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra in 1993. It is located in Bhubaneswar. 287 The aim of this school is to preserve l and popularise the rich culture of Odissi dance by maintaining high standards of performance and professionalism. Oxford Odissi Centre This centre was founded by Baisali l Mohanty in 2015 in the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. The aim of this centre is to promote and educate Odissi classical dance outside India. This centre also conducts Odissi dance l workshops in other leading institutions like University of Cambridge, London School of Economics, King’s College, London, University of Edinburgh and University of Manchester. Artists of Odisha Gopal Chhotray He was born in 1916 in Puranagarh village of Jagatsinghpur district of Odisha. He is credited to be one of the chief architects of Modern Oriya theatre. He wrote many stage plays and adaptations of Oriya novels. His first work was Sahadharmini in 1942. He received Padma Shri in 2002. He also got many awards like Odisha Sahitya Akademi Awards (1976), Sahitya Akademi Awards (1982), Sarala Award (2000), etc. He died on 22nd January, 2003. Kelucharan Mohapatra He was born in 1926 in Raghurajpur, Puri district in Odisha. He was a renowned Indian classical dancer, guru and exponent of Odissi dance. 288 His contribution is very great as he popularised the Odissi dance form through out the world. He was also the first person to receive the Padma Vibhushan from Odisha state. He also received other awards like Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, (1966), Padma Shri (1974), Padma Bhushan (1988), Padma Vibhushan (2000). He died on 7th April, 2004. Akshaya Mohanty He was born in 1934 in Kendrapara district of Odisha. He was also known as Khoka Bhai. He was an Indian singer, lyricist, composer, musician and writer. His contribution can be seen in Odia Bhajans, Odissi songs, Folk songs, film and non-film modern light songs in Odisha on contemporary themes and also in ballads which are based on popular legends in Odisha. He received Jayadeva award, the highest State Award for best playback singer (seven times). He died on 17th November, 2002. Prafulla Kar He was born in 1939 in Puri district. He is a famous Oriya musician, singer, lyricist, writer and columnist. He have been honoured by many awards like Jayadeva Award (2004), Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Award (2009), Kadambini Award (2012), Padma Shri Award (2015), etc. Sonal Mansingh She was born in 1942. She is an Indian classical dancer and Guru in Bharatnatyam and Odissi dancing style. She has received many awards like Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1987), Padma Bhushan (1992), Padma Vibhushan (2003). She is the second women dancer in India to receive Padma Vibhushan’, India’s second highest Civilian award, after Balasaraswati. Gangadhar Pradhan He was born in 1948 in Parikula in Puri district of Odisha. He was a renowned Odissi exponent, classical dancer and choreographer of Odisha. He established the Konark Natya Mandap in Konark in Puri district in 1986. He is one of the founders of Odisha Dance Academy. He also established Chandra Shekhar Kala Mandir in 1992 in order to promote Odishan art and culture. He had a huge list of awards like State Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1993), Nrutya Pratibha Samman (2001), Nrutyamani Award (2005), Padma Shri (2008), etc. Arabinda Muduli He was born in 1961 in Khordha district of Odisha. He was an Indian Odia musician, singer and lyricist. He was a disciple of Bhikari Bal (Bhajan Samrat of Odisha). He only sung Bhajans in his life. He was honoured by a certificate of appreciation by Mumbai Odia Mahasangh in 2013. He died on 1st March, 2018. Music and Dance of Odisha Sona Mohapara She was born in 1976 in Cuttack district of Odisha. She is an Indian singer, music composer and lyricist. She has done many concerts across the world and also worked in albums, singles, concert webcasts, music videos, bollywood films, etc. She has sung many famous songs like ‘Lori’ (Family), ‘Ambarsariya’ (Fukrey), Dil Aaj Kal’ (Purani Jeans), etc. Saswat Joshi He was born in 1984 in Titlagarh town in Balangir district of Odisha. He is an Indian classical dancer, model, exponent of the Odissi dancing style and choreographer. 289 He travelled and performed Odissi dance in many countries in order to popularise Odissi as an Indian classical dance. He received many awards like Sangeet Ratna from Bangiya Sankrutik Sangha, Rabindra Bharati University, the youth inspiration award from the Odisha Diary, etc. Baisali Mohanty She was born in 1994 in Puri district of Odisha. She is an Indian classical dancer, author, choreographer and analyst of foreign and public policy. She founded the Oxford Odissi Centre’ that provides training and promotes Odissi dance in University of Oxford and other leading institutions in United Kingdom. She received awards like an award from India’s National Commission for Women at New Delhi (2013) and Arya Award in 2017 for her contribution to Indian classical dance. 290

Places like Dhabaleswar (Cuttack) and Barkul (Khordha) are highly visited by tourists for such adventurous activities. Football It is one of the major sports in Odisha. Football sport is administered by the Football Association of Odisha (FAO). The Odisha Women’s Football Team provided many players to the India Women’s National Football team. The state also has Odisha men’s football team. Important football players from Odisha are Susmita Malik, Rakesh Oram, Supriya Routray, Manisha Panna, Proloy Shah, etc. Field Hockey It is the most popular sport of Odisha. The Odisha Government has become the first Government in India which has sponsored a national team of this sport. Odia Hockey Team is the state’s field hockey team. Its home grounds are Biju Patnaik Hockey Stadium in Rourkela and Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar. The Hockey Odisha team has provided many renowned players to Indian Men’s National Field Hockey Team and India Women’s National Field Hockey Team. Important players are Anupa Barla, Binita Toppo, Birendra Lakra, Dilip Tirkey, Ignace Tirkey, Prabodh Tirkey, etc. Hockey World Cup 2018 The 14th Hockey World Cup was held in the city of Bhubaneswar, Odisha from 28th November to 16th December, 2018. Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar hosted the inaugration ceremony that witnessed the biggest drone flying show in India. Organising this tournament was a huge opportunity for Odisha to celebrate the sport of Hockey. This is the third time, India has hosted the tournament. Other hosts were Bombay (1982) and New Delhi (2010). The tournament was won by Belgium while India reached till the quarter finals. Rugby It is another major sports of Odisha. Rugby Football is administered by the Odisha Rugby Football Association. Odisha has many Rugby teams like Odisha Women’s Rugby Union teams, Odisha Women’s Rugby seven teams and Odisha Men’s Rugby seven teams. The state has hosted the Asia Rugby Women’s Championship which played from 26th to 28th October, 2018. Trekking Odisha is an ideal place for trekkers and mountain lovers. One can trek-up to a height of about 1600 m. Some of the best trekking routes in Odisha are Gandhamardan Trek, Mahendragiri Trek and Nilagiri Trek. The time period between October-January is the ideal time for trekking in Odisha. Wrestling It is considered as one of the most ancient and oldest sports and has glorious past. The state participates in many tournaments at National Level, e.g. in the ‘National Arm Wrestling Sports in Odisha Tournament’ (2015) Odisha won 10 medals. Prominent wrestlers of the state are Gautam Kumar Kahali, Chandra Behera, Sambit Nanda, etc. Traditional Sports in Odisha Kabaddi It is counted among the most common and widely played traditional sports. It is the game where one person plays against seven people. Kho Kho It is one of India’s very famous traditional game. This game is very popular in Odisha. It is also known as ‘Standing Game’. This is the sport where players chase and try to touch a person. Odisha Kho Kho Association is the governing body of Kho Kho in Odisha. (Rope Pulling) It is a Rassi Tana traditional game of Odisha. It is a contest of strength in which two teams tug on opposite ends of a rope, each trying to pull the other across a dividing line. Nadia Phinga (Coconut Throwing) This is a traditional game of Odisha. This is a game of throwing coconuts on land or even in water. One whose coconut covers the longest distance, is the one who wins. Khapara Dian This is a traditional game of Odisha. In this game, one has to jump with one leg and perform various tasks. Puchi It is another traditional game of Odisha which is a game dance of the state. It is played both in sitting and standing positions. Usually, this sport is played by young girls during moonlight nights of Hindu month of Ashwin. 309 Sword Fighting This is another traditional sport of the state. A sword fight is a battle between two-people, each with a sword and the goal is to defeat the opponent as fast as one can. A sword fight can be in sport, battle or fun. Paen Anba (Bringing Water) This traditional game is performed by both boys and girls of 5 to 8 years age group. It visualises the culinary tradition of Western Odisha. In this game, participants take water from pond or river and prepare different traditional food items symbolically. It is a traditional Machhasare Ghina game of Odisha. It represents the selling of fish by fisher women moving around the Para (settlements). Gedi It is a traditional game of Odisha. It is played by all adolescent, young and middle-aged. It is a totally ritual based game. Performance of this game started from Ratha Yatra, the second day of bright fortnight of Ashadh and continues till new moon of Bhadrapad. Ganthi Ganana It is a game performed during wedding ceremony by Kharial tribes of Sundargarh district. In this game, one of the Sians (senior and respectable person) asks everybody to tell the name of the nine-node of bamboo stick, which represents the names of their Gotra (lineage). The Cricket activities and events are managed by the Odisha Cricket Association. It is affiliated to the Board of Control for Cricket in India. This association started the local Twenty-20 tournament known as Odisha Premier League. The association is responsible to manage the Barabati Stadium for Cricket in Cuttack, Odisha Cricket Academy and Sachin Tendulkar Indoor Cricket Hall and many other grounds in the state. Football Association of Odisha The Football Association of Odisha is situated in Cuttack. It is the state governing body of football in the state. It is affiliated to the All India Football Association. It manages the Odisha Men’s Football Team as well as the Odisha Women’s Football Team. It started various tournaments like the Football League, Kalinga Cup, Gati Krushna Memorial Football League, The Sahani Cup, BC Roy Football Memorial Tournament, etc. Sports and Youth Services Department, Odisha This department was set up by the State Government of Odisha in Bhubaneswar. It aims to encourage young players and support their participation and involvement. The department provides opportunities to the young persons for economic and social development. It also organises national integration championships, exchange programmes, youth leadership championship at district and state levels. Hockey Odisha The Hockey Odisha is the state governing body of Hockey in Odisha. It was earlier known as the Hockey Association of Odisha. It is affiliated to Hockey India, Odisha Olympic Association and Odisha Council of Sports. It is located in Barabati Stadium in Cuttack district. Odisha Olympic Association It is the governing body of sports in the state of Odisha. Its headquarters is located in Cuttack district. The association is responsible for selecting athletes to represent the country at national and international level games like Olympic Games, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and National Games of India. Maharaja Sriram Chandra Bhanj Deo He was born in 1870 in Baripada in Mayurbhanj. He was an enlightened ruler of Princely State of Mayurbhanj. He formally conquered the throne on 15th August, 1892. He worked for upliftment of Mayurbhanj and implemented various welfare schemes designed to help the people. He presided over the first meeting of Utkal Sammilani on 3rd December, 1933. He was a leading freedom fighter, a social reformer and an active participant in the Non-Cooperation Movement. He led the national freedom movement in Sambalpur region. He was a founding member of the National School of Sambalpur. As the Chairman of Sambalpur Municipality, he received Gandhiji at Sambalpur in 1928. He is also credited to organise a mass movement against illiteracy and untouchability. He died in the year 1936. Pandit Gopabandhu Das He was born in 1877 in Suando village in Puri district of Odisha. He was a social reformer, worker, political activist, journalist, poet and essayist. He was popularly known as the Gandhi of Odisha, and Utkalamani ( Jewel of Utkal/Odisha). He greatly contributed in the formation of a separate province of Odisha. He is credited to establish Satyabadi School, popularly known as Satyabadi Bakul Bana Bidyalaya, at Sakhigopala in Puri district. The students of this school were proved to be energetic fighters against the British power. Mahatma Gandhi conferred him by saying, ‘‘Gopabandhu was one of the Noblest Sons of Odisha’’. He died in the year 1928. Nilakantha Das He was born in 1884 in Puri district of Odisha (Bengal Presidency, British India). He was an orator, social reformer, speaker, writer, politician and a freedom fighter. 348 He inspired the youth to fight against untouchables and other social evils. His epics are considered as masterpiece of Odia language. He was honoured by the Padma Bhushan in 1960. He died in 1967. Parbati Giri She was born in 1926 in Bargarh district of Odisha. She was a prominent female freedom fighter of Odisha, who took part in the Indian freedom struggle. From 1942, she campaigned for the ‘Quit India Movement’, and was imprisoned many times by the British. After Independence, she served the nation socially and opened an orphanage at Paikural village, in Bargarh district and devoted her life for the welfare of orphans. She died in the year 1995. Political Personalities Biswanath Das He was born in 1889 in Ganjam district (Madras Presidency, British India) of Odisha. He was an eminent politician, leader, freedom fighter, able statesman and remarkable administrator. He was elected as the President of the Ganjam District Board in the year 1920. He joined the Non-Cooperation Movement in response to the call of Mahatma Gandhi in 1921, after giving-up his law practice. He continued to be a member of Madras Legislative Assembly from 1921 to 1930. He was the Prime Minister of the Odisha Province of British India from 1937-39. He led the Peasant Movement and fought for the creation of a separate Odisha province. He was elected to Lok Sabha in 1950 and became the President of Utkal Pradesh Congress Committee. He served as the Governor of Uttar Pradesh 1962-67. He became the Chief Minister of Odisha from 1971-72. He died in the year 1984. Maharaja Krushna Chandra Gajapati He was born in 1892 in Paralakhemundi in Puri district of Odisha. He was considered as the Architect of Independent Modern Odisha. He was the great freedom fighter and the first Prime Minister of Odisha from 1941-1944. He was also one of the founding fathers of the Indian Constitution and a member of the Constituent Assembly of India. He attended the First Round Table Conference in London on 16th November, 1930 wherein he made an appeal for creating a separate province of Odisha on the basis of language and homogeneity. He was also a member of old Madras Legislative Council, a member of Royal Commission of Agriculture and a member of Odisha Legislative Assembly. He died in the year 1974. Harekrushna Mahatab He was born in 1899 in Agarpada village in Bhadrak district. He was a leader of the Indian National Congress, a renowned personality of Indian Independence Movement and politician. He was popularly known as Utkal Keshari. His political career started in 1921, when he took part in ‘Pada Yatra’ started by Mahatma Gandhi. Historical and Other Famous Personalities He became the first Chief Minister of Odisha from 1946-1950. He started a magazine named ‘Jhankar’ in Odia language and a children’s magazine named ‘Minabajar’. He was the founder of the Prajatantra Prachar Samiti and started Prajatantra, a weekly magazine in 1923 at Balasore. This magazine was later known as the ‘Daily Prajatantra’. He was instrumental in shifting the capital from Cuttack to Bhubaneswar. In 1983, he was honoured by the ‘Sahitya Academy Award’ for the third volume of his famous work ‘Gaon Majlis’. He died in the year 1987. Raja Artatran Deo He was born in the year 1900. In 1921, he became the Raja of Khariar (present day Nuapada district). He was a great patron of art, culture and education, sportsman of distinction, member of many committees and organisations. He patronised Beer Bikram Theatre of Khariar, the first permanent Odia stage in the state. He was a nominated member of Odisha Advisory Council. He was elected to Odisha Legislative Assembly in 1937 and 1946 from Khariar Assembly Constituency. He played a pivotal role in formation of Odisha as a separate province in the year 1936. Due to his leadership Khariar Zamindari merged with the state of Odisha leading to full statehood. He died in the year 1946. Biju Patnaik He was born in 1916 in Cuttack district of Odisha. He was an Indian politician and businessman. of Odisha 349 He got training of pilot and with the starting of the Second World War he joined the Royal Indian Air Force and later became head of air transport command (1940-42). He became the Chief Minister of Odisha twice, first in 1961-1963 and second in 1990-1995. He is also credited to make strong the basic infrastructure of the state through many projects. Some of these are Port of Paradip, Odisha Aviation Centre, Bhubaneswar Airport, the Cuttack–Jagatpur Mahanadi Highway Bridge, Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, Bhubaneswar, NALCO (National Aluminium Company), Talcher Thermal Power Station, Balimela Hydel Project, HAL Sunabeda. He also established the Kalinga Cup in Football. He died in the year 1997. Chintamani Panigrahi He was born in 1922 in Puri district of Odisha. He was an Indian Independence Movement activist, a political and social leader from Odisha. He became a member of 2nd Lok Sabha in 1957 from Puri Constituency. He was re-elected to be Lok Sabha in 1967, 1971, 1980 and 1984 from Bhubaneswar Constituency. 350 He served at various posts like Minister of State for Home Affairs from 1986-88, Minister of State in the Ministry of Defence from 1988-89 and also served as the Governor of Manipur from 1989–1993. He died in the year 2000. Nandini Satpathy She was born in 1931 in Pithapur, Cuttack district of Odisha. She was an Indian politician and author. She was the first woman Chief Minister of Odisha from 1972-1973. She was a writer in the Odia language and authored many poems and short stories. She was conferred with Sahitya Bharati Samman for the translation of the famous novel ‘Lajja’ into Odia language. She is also the founder of Odisha Women’s Relief Committee. She was elected twice to Rajya Sabha from Congress party. She died in the year 2006. Naveen Patnaik He was born on 16th October, 1946 in Cuttack district. He is an Indian politician and writer. His father Biju Patnaik was a great freedom fighter and former Chief Minister of Odisha. In early life, he was a writer and stayed away from politics. But after the death of his father, he entered politics. From the year 2000, he is serving as Chief Minister in Odisha. He is the 14th Chief Minister of Odisha. Odisha has developed in the field like science and technology, economy, etc, in these years. He also has written books namely A Second Paradise, A Desert Kingdom and The Garden of Life. Shri Prasanna Acharya He was born on 8th August, 1949 in Bargarh district of Odisha. He is an politician from Odisha. He was a member of the 13th and the 14th Lok Sabha of India. He represented the Sambalpur Constituency of Odisha and is a member of the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) political party. He is the member of Parliament of Rajya Sabha, since 2016. Tathagata Satpathy He was born on 1st April, 1956 in Cuttack district of Odisha. He is a politician from Odisha. He has been a member of Lok Sabha for 4 times (in 12th, 14th, 15th and 16th Lok Sabha) since 2004. He was re-elected for the fourth time as a member of Lok Sabha in 2014. He represents the Dhenkanal Constituency and is a member of the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) political party. Historical and Other Famous Personalities Miscellaneous Personalities Jatin Das He was born in 1914 at Baripada in Mayurbhanj district of Odisha. He is an Indian painter and sculptor. He has been painting for 50 years. He has received many awards like Utkala Award (Kolkata) in 2006, Bharat Nirman Award in 2007, Padma Bhushan in 2012 and so on. He also wrote many books like The Art of Jatin Das, and Poems by Jatin Das. Kailash Chandra Meher He was born in 1954 in Sonepur district of Odisha. He is an Indian artist, social activist, painter and inventor. He is a famous painter of contemporary ‘Modern Art’ paintings and traditional Tussar Pattachitra paintings of Odisha. For the upliftment of the forest girls and women of (Kalahandi-Balangir- Koraput) districts of Odisha, he has started many social organisations such as, ‘Indian Art and Craft Academy for Women’, ‘Indira Gandhi Women Weavers Co–operative Society Limited’, ‘Bhartiya Hastakala Industrial Co-operative Society Limited’, ‘Handicraft and Handloom Museum and Service Centre for Women’. He has been conferred by many awards like of Odisha 351 Orissa Lalit Kala Academy Award (1979 and 1985), UNESCO CCI Seal of Excellence for Handicrafts’(2005), Padma Shri Award (2013) and Odisha Living Legend Award (2013) and many others. Mansi Pradhan She was born on 4th October, 1962 in Khordha district of Odisha. She is an Indian Women’s Right activist and author. In 2009 she launched the Honour for Women National Compaign, which was a nation wide movement to end violence against women in India. In 2014 this campaign released a four-point charter of demand for all the State Governments of the country for the security of women and girls in the country. She has been conferred by many awards like Rani Lakshmi Bai, Stree Shakti Puraskar (2014), Outstanding Women Award (2011). Sudarshan Pattnaik He was born on 15th April, 1977 in Puri district of Odisha. He is an Indian Sand Artist from Odisha. He is famous for his sand sculptures at Bandrabhan, Hoshangabad and Puri. He has been conferred by many awards and honours some of these are Padma Shri (2014), Sarala Award (2008), Award for Excellence and so on. Jayanta Meher He was born on 3rd June, 1986 in Sonepur district of Odisha. He is a famous artist of Odisha Pattachitra painting. He is the son of famous artist Kailash Chandra Meher. He was conferred by the Master Craftsman National Award in 2001. 352
